findings.summary: The keyword-only trigger misses records-measure changes that the snapshot's own history shows, and the plan rejects the narrower signal: a change to the measure-only modules.
findings.evidence: HISTORY.txt line 109: commit 5724053 (2026-11-10) 'Report per-rule reading refusal counts in status; flag rules over 30%' changes a records-computed refusal rate but says 'refusal counts', which is not on the list. Line 441 says 'wasted work' and 'landed time', and line 1233 says 'time spent'. HISTORY.txt lines 86-99 and 101 are commits that changed crates/athena-data/src/records/throughput.rs with subjects naming no measure. Decision 7 rejects a path trigger because it 'would flag every edit to a file such as status.rs', but status/throughput.rs and records/throughput.rs hold only measure code. Bare 'throughput' also matches unrelated readings about CI or drain throughput. Fix: Trigger on the measure-only module paths in the deliverables (crates/athena-data/src/records/throughput.rs, crates/athena-core/src/status/throughput.rs, plus the functions that compute the keep rule and the per-rule refusal counts, located by reading the code) as well as on words. Widen the word list from the measures' real names (refusal count(s), refusal share, landed time, time spent, wasted work) and narrow bare 'throughput' to phrases about records (e.g. 'throughput section', 'throughput review'). Add a corpus case rebuilt from 5724053 that expects Refuse, and a reading.rs test for the path trigger.
findings.location: Approach and Decision 7 (match measures only in summary and criteria, a fixed RECORDS_MEASURE_PHRASES list)

findings.summary: The dependents list leaves out drain, which uses check_reading_text to decide whether a request that is queued and already read stays in the queue.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs:114-123: a proposed request stays queued and runs without a new read when its stored reading passes check_reading_text. A proposed request whose stored reading fails a reading check is left out of the queue and waits for a person to run `athena go`. The test is crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs:4407-4451. The plan's entry names only check-reading, the verification replay and the steward. So after this change, stored readings on queued measure requests (for example those that Hestia's throughput review queues, HISTORY.txt line 709) would drop out of drain quietly. Fix: Add drain.rs (and plan, which runs the same pass) to the dependents list with the effect stated: a stored reading of a measure change with no real-records criterion leaves the queue until someone re-reads it or runs `athena go`. Say whether that is intended. Either add a drain test with such a stored reading, or explain why the existing drain.rs:4407 test covers it.
findings.location: Dependents, entry 'readings newly refused when stored readings are replayed'

findings.summary: The suggested example names `status --snapshot`, whose output is the measure being changed, so it is not an independent source for the expected range.
findings.evidence: briefs.rs:665-666: `status --snapshot` 'prints the job counts, the history summary and the throughput section'. That is the output of the code under change. The request requires a range 'taken from an independent source (git log, recorded check durations)'. Fix: In the refusal text and the CHANGELOG example, take the expected range from `history.json` commit times or landing record timestamps, and present `status --snapshot` only as the real output that is checked against that range.
findings.location: Decision 5 and Step 2 (refusal text example using `status --snapshot`)

findings.summary: A `git diff -U0` of reader.rs cannot show 'exactly one added rule line', because the plan also shortens existing entries, which appear as added lines.
findings.evidence: Decision 2 shortens several existing READING_RULES entries in the same file, so the diff will contain several '+' rule lines. Fix: Rest criterion 1 on the test assertion (READING_RULES.len() goes from 11 to 12, and exactly one line names real records, an independent source and an expected range), and use the diff only as a supplement.

findings.summary: The demonstration leaves open whether the history.json variant trips check_environment_reach. The code answers this.
findings.evidence: ENV_LOCATED_SOURCES (surveys.rs:561-567) lists only records branch, athena/records, git history, git log and commit history. 'real records' and 'history.json commit times' match none of them. Fix: State that the history.json variant needs no Environment: assumption, and assert gate_refuser(..) == None for it with no assumption added.

summary: The plan is concrete and its code references check out: refusing_check (checks.rs:518) with the step! line for check_history_fixture (538), changes_code_with_behavior_criterion (surveys.rs:237), has_phrase/straight_lowercase, ENV_LOCATED_SOURCES (561), READING_RULES [&str; 11] (reader.rs:287), the planner Report string (planner.rs:134), the 3150 reader-section limit (briefs.rs:3558), the replay helpers and the evidence snapshot, which run/mod.rs:1144 writes on every dispatch. The files outside the deliverable list (Athena's findings 1-4) are justified. Two problems need fixing. First, soundness: the trigger is a fixed keyword list, and the snapshot's own history shows a measure change it misses. Commit 5724053 (2026-11-10, 'per-rule reading refusal counts… flag rules over 30%') is a records-computed refusal rate written as 'refusal counts', and two commits that changed records/throughput.rs name no measure at all. The plan also rejects the narrower path trigger on the measure-only modules. Second, the dependents list leaves out drain. Drain keeps a request that is queued and already read only if its stored reading passes check_reading_text, so readings of measure changes would quietly drop out of the queue. Minor issues: the example 'independent' source, the criterion-1 diff demonstration, and an open hedge in criterion 4.
